contexts.text: In abundance of all Knowledges and celestial goods, which is not to hunger ().
The love which was the veriest life of the Lord, is signified by He hungered... ().
(Those who hunger, a class of the good.)

With those in the affection of good, the good with them longs for good as one hungry longs for bread; but with those in the affection of truth, the good with them longs for truth, as one thirsty for water.
By one hungry, the Angels perceive those who from affection long for good. AC 4958, Explained.
When these things are hungered for they yield better nourishment.
They called those the hungry to whom they would give to eat.
The hungry () = one who longs for good.
They shall not hunger () = that they shall not lack good.
The hungry, here () are those who elsewhere are called the poor, thus who have not bread and water... that is, who do not know good and truth, but still long for them.
To hunger and not be satisfied () = not to receive the good and truth of faith.
[Swedenborg footnote 2.] To hunger and thirst - to long for the Knowledges of good and truth, by means of which there is introduction into the Church and Heaven.
The little children of the Africans there frequently... say that they are hungry... from which it is evident that spiritual hunger, which is a longing to know genuine truths, operates this. SE 6095.
As no food from Heaven is given the idle... they begin to be hungry...
Under Food, see this reference.
That famine, or hunger = a longing to know and understand the truths and goods of the Church Illustrated.
They shall hunger no more, nor thirst any more () = that after this they shall not lack goods and truths. Explained. AE 480.
To hunger = to long for good.
Those who hunger and thirst = those who are continually longing for truths, and to be perfected by means of them. AE 118:5.
Those who hunger = those who long for Knowledges; such as were the gentiles, who accepted the Lord and the doctrine from Him.
To empty out the hungering soul () = to deprive of the Knowledges of good those who long for them...
To hunger and not be satisfied = to be deprived. ( = not to be found, and if found still not to be received. AE 600:13. AE 617:29.)
To hunger = the deprivation of good.
To hunger = to be deprived of the good of love.
To hunger = to want to know.
To hunger = to be in the lack of (the Knowledges of good and truth); and also to be deprived of them.
Those who hunger = those who are in ignorance of the Knowledges of good and truth, and still are in the longing.
The young lions which shall be in need and shall hunger () = those who know and are wise from themselves: to be in need and to hunger = that they have neither truth nor good.
The hungering soul = those who long for goods.
Those who hunger = those who long for.

To hunger and thirst = to hunger and thirst for the things of eternal life, or which give that life, which in general have relation to the good of love and the truth of faith; to hunger, to the good of love; and to thirst, to the truth of faith.
Principles of falsity and the love of evil... take away all spiritual hunger and thirst.
To hunger, here () = to come to the Lord... To come to the Lord is to do His precepts.
To hunger and thirst = to be in spiritual ignorance and need.
It is said of the Lord that He hungered and thirsted, and by these words is meant that from Divine love He willed and longed for the salvation of the human race. Illustrated. AE 617:19.
To hunger, when said of the Lord, = to long for good in the Church.
To hunger and thirst, in the Word... = spiritual hunger and thirst, which are the deprivation, lack, and ignorance of the Knowledges of truth and good, and at the same time a longing for them.
Spiritual hunger and thirst are the affection and longing for good and truth.
Not to hunger for bread () = not to long for good, which [state] exists with those who are in falsities and evils...
The soul of the hungering = the understanding of good.
They who are in the lack of truth and good, and long for them, are meant in the Word by those who hunger.
